THE VENDORING CHOICE IS NOW EVIDENCED, not asserted. Read both implementations: solid-js 1.x mergeProps resolves a key with 'if (v !== undefined) return v', @solidjs/signals 2.x merge with 'if (property in s) return s[property]'. Presence, not definedness — so a caller-supplied prop that happens to be undefined erases a declared default under merge. Both call sites here are defaults-then-props, so plain merge was unsafe at BOTH, as form-e0p.2 predicted. The mechanism is now cited in merge-objects.ts's doc comment. Also verified mergeObjects works against a Solid 2 props proxy: propTraps implements getOwnPropertyDescriptor (returning a getter) and ownKeys, so Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors sees the keys and reactivity survives.

The finding is recorded at the top of tests/utils/reactive.ts as required (see f8y.1 for why that file exists at all).

CONTRACT 5 (update() never before mount()) — covered, but by the EXISTING suite rather than a new test, and that is deliberate. It cannot be pinned by a bespoke black-box test: the violation happens inside createField before any handle to the FieldApi exists (the children callback runs after the render effect's synchronous first pass), so there is no interception point without mocking form-core. Instead the guard's removal was MEASURED: deleting 'if (!mounted) return' from createField.tsx and createFormGroup.tsx fails 8 tests in createForm.test.tsx (the five validate-on-change/blur/async tests plus the three array-field-name tests). So the regression guard exists and is strong; it just already lived in the suite. Recorded rather than duplicated.

THREE CONTRACTS WERE NON-DISCRIMINATING WHEN FIRST WRITTEN, and the traps are now comments in the file: asserting on an input the user typed into passes either way (needs a separate mirror element); counting children-callback invocations always reports 1 (Solid runs it once and re-runs only inner expressions); and a dev-diagnostic assertion over STATIC options passes with every untrack deleted.

BYPRODUCT FINDING, and a correction to this branch: untrack() around the constructor seed does NOT silence STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED — measured at 4 either way. untrack stops a read from SUBSCRIBING, not from being reported. The comments in createForm/createField/createFormGroup claimed otherwise and are fixed. The untrack that does earn its keep is the one around api.update: 3 diagnostics per push, which is what contract 2 now guards.
